meta.subtitle: 12x Samsung 96 GB DDR5-6400 (1.15 TB) + HPL FP64 - Tyrone MDI300
meta.platform: Tyrone MDI300 / 2x Intel Xeon 6730P (64C/128T, Granite Rapids)

executive_summary: 3-hour memory validation of 12x Samsung 96 GB DDR5-6400 Registered ECC DIMMs (1.15 TB total) in server 172.16.11.41 (Tyrone MDI300, dual Intel Xeon 6730P Granite Rapids), plus an HPL (High-Performance Linpack) FP64 compute campaign. Two memory phases: a 2-hour stress-ng --vm-method all --verify sweep across an 832 GB working set, and a 30-minute memtester burn locking 1088 GB (96.0% of RAM).

All 12 DIMMs were detected by BMC, BIOS and kernel; modules ran at their full rated 6400 MT/s (no platform downclock - Intel Granite Rapids natively supports 1DPC DDR5-6400); EDAC stayed clean; zero memtester failures and zero machine-check events. The CPU reached full 3.8 GHz max turbo (3792 MHz) - healthy, unlike the sibling .19 unit firmware-locked at 500 MHz.

HPL sustained 5.11 TFLOPS FP64 (N=340000, ~80% RAM, 8x8 grid, 64 MPI ranks) = 69% of the ~7.4 TFLOPS theoretical peak (the practical netlib HPL ceiling). A near-full-memory run (N=370000, 93% RAM, 1.10 TiB matrix) PASSED at 4.55 TFLOPS with no OOM. The server is validated for production memory- and compute-bound workloads.

comparison.caption: MDI300 (Xeon 6730P, SNC2) vs the EPYC 9135 reference - both 1.15 TB DDR5-6400, both pass.
comparison.notes: Intel runs the modules at full rated 6400 MT/s (no clamp); AMD's EPYC Turin 1DPC clamps to 6000. Aggregate STREAM is comparable (~417 vs ~443 GB/s). EPYC has stronger single-thread bandwidth (Zen 5); Intel SNC2 (4 NUMA nodes) shows a larger NUMA-remote penalty by design. This .41 MDI300 is healthy at full 3.8 GHz turbo - unlike the sibling .19 unit firmware-locked at 500 MHz.

sel_status: BMC SEL: 0 new entries during the campaign (last entry pre-test).
dmesg_status: 0 machine-check events in the 2h47m window. Intel EDAC enumerated 16 memory controllers; per-DIMM counters all CE=0 / UE=0. turbostat shows cores at 3792 MHz (full max turbo) under load - no thermal or firmware throttle.
findings: All 12 Samsung 96 GB DDR5-6400 modules are electrically and structurally healthy: 2 hours of write-and-verify across 52 stress-ng patterns plus 30 minutes at 96.0% RAM residency (1.09 TB pinned) produced zero ECC errors at controller and DIMM level.

BIOS trains every module at full rated 6400 MT/s - no platform downclock on this Granite Rapids board. Kernel logged 0 machine-check events; BMC SEL added 0 new entries; mlock() succeeded on all 64 memtester workers (96% of RAM pinned without reclaim/OOM/swap).

CPU runs at full 3792 MHz under load (matching the 3800 MHz max turbo) - no thermal or firmware throttle, unlike the sibling MDI300 at 172.16.13.19 which was locked at 500 MHz. Bandwidth and HPL here are therefore representative.

Compute (HPL FP64): 5.11 TFLOPS sustained (N=340000, ~80% RAM, NB=384, 8x8 grid, 64 MPI ranks, 85 min) = 69% of the ~7.4 TFLOPS theoretical peak - the practical ceiling for netlib HPL 2.3 + MKL. BIOS Performance + Turbo lifted the large-N result 4.92 -> 5.11 TFLOPS (+4%); SNC2-on is ~10% faster than SNC-off for this rank-per-core layout.

Max-memory HPL: N=370000 (a 1.10 TiB matrix, 93% RAM) PASSED in 2h04m at 4.55 TFLOPS with no OOM or swap - TOP500-style near-full-memory stability. ~80% RAM is the HPL sweet spot; N>=400000 would require the 2 TB (8x 256 GB) DIMM configuration.
recommendations: Modules cleared for production: no DIMM action required; the 1.15 TB configuration is qualified for memory- and compute-bound workloads (in-memory DBs, AI inference, HPC, virtualization).
For higher HPL efficiency (~5.9-6.6 TFLOPS, 80-90%), use Intel's oneMKL LINPACK binary instead of netlib HPL (the binary is the limiter at 69%); keep SNC2 enabled for production and benchmarking.
Populate the remaining 4 channels per socket (full 16-of-16) to push aggregate STREAM beyond ~500 GB/s and unlock the full Granite Rapids memory subsystem.
Optional 8-hour soak; enable BIOS patrol scrub (RAS) and install rasdaemon for continuous per-DIMM error history.
Use this healthy .41 MDI300 as the reference to diagnose the .19 unit's 500 MHz frequency lock - same SKU, so a BIOS/microcode diff should identify the fix.
